entries.title: OSCP+ Exam Guide
entries.access_note: Public help-centre article returned by the search; no sign-in indicated.
entries.evidence: Query: 'OffSec OSCP+ exam guide help center scoring changes December 1 2026 equated scaled scoring' (help.offsec.com, offsec.com). Result title 'OSCP+ Exam Guide' at this URL; per the search summary the guide still lists the 60/40 point split (three standalone machines and one Active Directory set) while an older notice, 'OSCP Exam Change' (offsec.com/blog/oscp-exam-structure/), describes a 70/30 structure with a bonus; the exam text of the guide itself was not shown. Other results: 'OSCP+ Exam FAQ' (help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/4412170923924-OSCP-Exam-FAQ) and 'OSCP+ Candidate Handbook' (help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/40393367449108-OSCP-Candidate-Handbook).
entries.version: as listed 2026-11-18; the structure statements conflict between pages
entries.notes: Re-read the live guide, FAQ and handbook before any exam booking; the plan notes AI chatbot and automation restrictions, which no search result here confirmed (see plan_fact_checks). Ordinary lab use on D30 is not bound by exam rules; the benchmark itself forbids AI assistance by the plan's own rule. estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: OSCP+ Equated Scaled Scoring FAQ
entries.access_note: Public help-centre article returned by the search; no sign-in indicated.
entries.evidence: Same query as w06-offsec-oscp-exam-guide. Result title 'OSCP+ Equated Scaled Scoring FAQ' at this URL; result text (with the OffSec blog 'OSCP+ Scoring Update: What You Need to Know', offsec.com/blog/oscp-grading-update/): exams starting before 2026-12-01 08:00 GMT keep the fixed passing score of 70; exams starting on or after it pass at 400 on a scaled 100 to 500 range; the raw points needed for 400 depend on the exam set; past attempts are not rescored; point values, proof requirements, documentation standards, format, time limits, proctoring and the report deadline are unchanged.
entries.version: effective for exams starting on or after 2026-12-01 08:00 GMT
entries.notes: Do not use a fixed 70-point target for an exam on or after 2026-12-01 (plan section 4). estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: Nibbles (Easy)
entries.access_note: help.hackthebox.com 'HTB Labs Subscriptions' (search result, 2026-11-18): the Free plan covers 20 active Machines; retired Machines come with VIP+ (25 USD per month or 223 USD per year) or HTB PRO (49 USD per month or 490 USD per year). The machine page is marked retired in the search summary.
entries.evidence: Query: 'hackthebox.com machines "Legacy (Easy)" OR "Blue (Easy)" OR "Jerry (Easy)" OR "Nibbles (Easy)" retired machine' (hackthebox.com). First result, title 'Nibbles (Easy)' at this URL; the page is marked retired; Linux.
entries.version: retired per the page label as seen 2026-11-18
entries.notes: Midpoint rule from the plan: one unknown target, no AI assistance, no full spoilers; read no write-up before the time limit. The machine page description names the vulnerability class, so the assigner (not the learner) draws the target and the learner sees the name and operating system only. Never publish a solution. HTB rule (Hack The Box Platform Rules, help.hackthebox.com/en/articles/12325897-hack-the-box-platform-rules, and the Acceptable Use Policy effective 2026-04-01, resources.hackthebox.com/hubfs/Legal/AUP.pdf): solutions, flags and write-ups of ACTIVE machines, challenges and Sherlocks must not be published; only retired content, Starting Point machines and Tier 0 Academy modules may be written about; a machine can be both active and expired, so confirm the page says retired. This file names retired machines only. estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: Blue
entries.access_note: No search result on tryhackme.com showed whether this room is free or Premium. tryhackme.com/free-rooms (search result 'Free Cyber Security Rooms & Labs') says 650+ rooms are free; help.tryhackme.com 'The AttackBox Explained': free users get up to one hour of AttackBox per day or can use their own machine through VPN. A TryHackMe 2026 blog on free red-team training (search summary) says the rooms it lists are free with an account but its room-to-URL mapping was not shown.
entries.evidence: Query: 'TryHackMe room Blue Kenobi Basic Pentesting Simple CTF Bounty Hacker beginner machines' (tryhackme.com). Result at this URL; result text: a Windows room about leveraging common misconfigurations, described as an educational series for complete beginners and not a boot2root CTF. The result title field is the generic 'TryHackMe'; the room name comes from the result text.
entries.notes: Guided room (task questions and hints), so a weak fit for the unknown-target rule; use only when no HTB retired machine is accessible and hide the task text. Other beginner rooms returned: Simple CTF (tryhackme.com/room/easyctf) and slug-only Ice, Steel Mountain, Alfred, HackPark. estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

plan_fact_checks.claim: HTB path duration estimates: Penetration Tester (CPTS) path 342 hours and SOC Analyst (CDSA) path 189 hours; they are platform averages, not course quotas (plan sections 4 and 16 item 1).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'HTB Academy Modules & Paths help article estimated hours ...' (help.hackthebox.com): 'Academy Modules & Paths' lists Penetration Tester (CPTS) 342 total estimated hours (42 days 6 hours) and SOC Analyst (CDSA) 189 hours (23 days 5 hours), an estimated day being an 8-hour session. The 342 + 189 = 531 total used in plan section 13 follows from these two figures.

plan_fact_checks.claim: HTB CPTS requires 100% of the Penetration Tester role path before the exam (plan sections 4, 13 and 16 item 2).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'HTB CPTS exam where to start requirements ...': the certification page 'HTB Certified Penetration Testing Specialist - HTB Academy' says the entire Penetration Tester job-role path (28 modules on that page) must be completed; a voucher with two attempts is separate (annual subscription includes one); report as PDF or ZIP up to 20 MB, uploaded within 10 days of entering the exam. The plan's where-to-start URL itself was not returned. Module count differs: 28 on the certification page, 27 on a course page.

plan_fact_checks.claim: OSCP+ scoring changes for exams on or after 2026-12-01 08:00 GMT: a scaled model replaces the fixed 70-point rule (plan sections 4, 13 and 16 item 3).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'OffSec OSCP+ exam guide help center scoring changes December 1 2026 equated scaled scoring' (help.offsec.com, offsec.com): 'OSCP+ Scoring Update: What You Need to Know' (offsec.com/blog/oscp-grading-update/) and 'OSCP+ Equated Scaled Scoring FAQ': attempts starting before 2026-12-01 08:00 GMT keep the fixed pass mark of 70; attempts on or after pass at 400 on a 100 to 500 scale, with the raw points needed depending on the exam set; past attempts are not rescored; format, time limits, proctoring, rules and report deadline are unchanged. Note: the 'OSCP+ Exam Guide' still lists a 60/40 split and an older notice lists 70/30 with a bonus, so the exam structure must be re-read live.

plan_fact_checks.claim: OSCP+ exam conditions restrict AI chatbot use and automation (plan sections 13 and 16 item 3).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: The OffSec results (exam guide, exam FAQ, candidate handbook, scoring FAQ) were returned, but none of the search summaries showed rule text on AI chatbots or automation, and the shared search budget ended before a dedicated query could be run. The statement is therefore neither confirmed nor contradicted; read the live guide and handbook.

plan_fact_checks.claim: The MITRE ATT&CK release current in November 2026 (plan section 4: review the October 2026 release).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: The query 'MITRE ATT&CK latest release version October 2026 release notes updates' could not run because the shared web search budget of the run was used up; no result on attack.mitre.org was seen. The learner must record the ATT&CK version number used on the live site.

plan_fact_checks.claim: HTB Penetration Tester path page exists at academy.hackthebox.com/path/preview/penetration-tester (plan section 5 week 6 core sites).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'HTB Academy Penetration Tester job role path modules tier list ...' (academy.hackthebox.com, help.hackthebox.com, hackthebox.com): result 'Penetration Tester Job Role Path' at that URL; the CPTS page says Tier 0 modules of the path are free. The modules used this week (Penetration Testing Process, Linux Privilege Escalation, Windows Privilege Escalation, Pivoting, Tunneling, and Port Forwarding, Documentation & Reporting) are returned with Easy or Medium difficulty labels; their tiers were not shown.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Solutions of ACTIVE Hack The Box machines, challenges and Sherlocks must not be published; only retired content may be (task rule for this file).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'Hack The Box platform rules writeups walkthrough active machines challenges Sherlocks must not be published retired only' (help.hackthebox.com, hackthebox.com): 'Hack The Box Platform Rules' (help.hackthebox.com/en/articles/12325897-hack-the-box-platform-rules), 'Streaming / Writeups / Walkthrough Guidelines' (help.hackthebox.com/en/articles/5188925-streaming-writeups-walkthrough-guidelines) and the Acceptable Use Policy effective 2026-04-01: retired Machines, Sherlocks and Challenges, Starting Point machines and Tier 0 Academy modules may be published; active ones and other Pro Labs must not; a machine can be both active and expired, so check it is officially retired.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Retired Hack The Box machines are not on the free plan (needed for the retired-machine pool of the unknown-target midpoint).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'Hack The Box HTB Labs Subscriptions free plan active machines retired machines VIP+ PRO price' (help.hackthebox.com, hackthebox.com): 'HTB Labs Subscriptions' says the Free plan covers 20 active Machines; VIP+ (25 USD per month or 223 USD per year) adds retired Machines and Challenges; PRO (49 USD per month or 490 USD per year) adds flagship Pro Labs. Retired machine pages found: Lame, Legacy, Jerry, Nibbles, Optimum, Bashed, Shocker and Cap (hackthebox.com/machines/<name>); no HTB page was found for Blue or Knife. HTB Academy and Labs subscriptions are billed separately.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Week 6 can draw the unknown target from pools of retired or beginner machines (plan section 5).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Eight retired HTB machine pages (Lame, Legacy, Jerry, Nibbles, Optimum, Bashed, Shocker, Cap) and TryHackMe beginner rooms (Basic Pentesting, Blue, Simple CTF) were returned. The HTB pool needs VIP+ (see the previous check); the TryHackMe rooms are guided, so they weaken the no-spoiler rule.

plan_fact_checks.claim: NIST SP 800-115 provides a rules-of-engagement template and a plan, execute, post-execute assessment structure (supports W06-Q01).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'NIST SP 800-115 Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment' (csrc.nist.gov): the 2008 final guide lists planning, execution and post-execution phases and appendices with a Rules of Engagement template. Whether a newer revision exists was not shown.

plan_fact_checks.claim: CVSS v4.0 is the current CVSS version and the specification is version 1.2 (support for the severity rationale).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'FIRST CVSS v4.0 specification document and user guide' (first.org): specification document 1.2 dated 2024-06-18, user guide dated 2025-11-16, FAQ states the current version is CVSS 4.0, released 2023-11-01; an examples PDF dated 2026-07-02 was also listed.

gaps: The shared web search budget of the run ended during this week's queries. Not searched: NVD and CVE record pages, CWE, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities, FIRST EPSS, Exploit-DB or searchsploit, PTES, GTFOBins, LOLBAS, sudoers and cron documentation, auditd documentation, OpenSSH ssh(1), Microsoft Learn service and DLL pages, NIST SP 800-41, CISA segmentation guidance, Chisel, Ligolo-ng, proxychains and socat documentation, Greenbone or Nessus documentation. The entries for NVD, CWE, MITRE ATT&CK, OpenBSD ssh(1) and the two Microsoft Learn pages are ASSUMED with their addresses unconfirmed today; those cross-referenced to the W01, W02 or W03 file are ASSUMED here and SEARCH_CHECKED there.
MITRE ATT&CK: the release current in November 2026 and the October 2026 release contents are not confirmed.
OSCP+ AI chatbot and automation restrictions are not confirmed by any search result seen.

Windows privilege escalation hosted scenario (D28, blocks B and C): the TryHackMe room name for tryhackme.com/room/windows10privesc is not confirmed (URL returned, no text); no free Windows-service-ACL scenario with a verified tier exists in this file; D28 block C therefore has no verified hosted exercise; the local G9 Windows VM is the primary route.

Segmentation theory (D29): no official segmentation or firewall-architecture reference (NIST SP 800-41, CISA) and no pivoting-tool documentation was verified; only the HTB module, three TryHackMe rooms and the Ubuntu firewall page are recorded.

Telemetry and defence blocks (D26 to D29): no CyberDefenders or LetsDefend exercise for privilege escalation, lateral movement or scanner false positives was searched; the only telemetry references are the Sysmon events page (W03 cross-reference) and the ATT&CK site (ASSUMED).
Scanner false positives (D26 block D): no Greenbone, Nessus or Nmap NSE documentation was verified.
HTB Academy tier is not shown for any of the six modules, so access is UNKNOWN; TryHackMe tier is not shown for any room (Wreath is described as possibly Premium because it is a network room).

Retired HTB machines need VIP+ or PRO; every pool entry is PAID. The free fallback is TryHackMe, whose rooms are guided and are weaker for the no-spoiler midpoint. No HTB page was found for Blue or Knife.

Hack The Box Sherlocks and HTB Starting Point machine pages are not used this week (only retired machines and an official beginner track may be named; Starting Point is recorded in W05 and earlier files).

HTB machine topics are deliberately not recorded (the page descriptions name the vulnerability class) so that the unknown-target draw stays blind; the assigner must read the machine page, the learner must not.
Provider-stated durations were not seen for any entry; every estimate is a planning figure.

INDEPENDENT RE-CHECK NOT RUN (2026-11-18): the checker could not run any web search because the shared 200-search budget of the turn was already used up. The 23 SEARCH_CHECKED labels, the access tiers (10 FREE, 4 PAID, 1 MIXED, 20 UNKNOWN) and the 11 plan_fact_checks results rest on the author's evidence only, and the 11 ASSUMED entries and the 1 UNVERIFIED entry (w06-thm-windows-privesc) are still unresolved. Re-run the checker with a fresh search budget before any day guide treats a URL, title, tier or fact check of this file as independently confirmed, and run the searches listed in the first gap (NVD, CWE, ATT&CK release, ssh(1), the two Microsoft Learn pages, the TryHackMe Windows PrivEsc room) first.
